sharepoint-quick-steps.title: Create a quick step for your list or library
sharepoint-quick-steps.notes: Quick steps are custom commands attached to a list or library in Microsoft Lists, SharePoint and Teams. They bundle a predefined action, for example running a Power Automate flow on the selected item or drafting an email to the people named in a column, so a user can trigger it from the command bar instead of opening the item. A quick step is created either by adding a new column of the Quick steps type or through the Integrate menu, where the maker picks an action under "For selected items", such as executing a flow, and gives it a name. Once an item or file is selected, quick steps show up at the top of the Automate menu and in the overflow menu, and they can act on a selected item or on the whole list depending on their type. Flows used this way must be manual flows or use a selected-item or selected-file trigger, and people who may not run the flow get an error unless the list or library is added as a co-owner. Creating or managing quick steps needs Edit permission on the library. Running them needs Read access for drafting an email, starting a Teams chat or executing a flow, but Edit access for setting a value or sending an approval request. Some actions need extra licensing, and the Ask Copilot action requires Copilot in SharePoint.

sharepoint-sharing-links.title: Shareable links in OneDrive and SharePoint (Anyone, People in your organization, Specific people)
sharepoint-sharing-links.notes: When a file or folder is shared in OneDrive or SharePoint, a link is created that carries the permission to the item. Microsoft Learn describes three link types. Anyone links work for whoever holds the link, with no sign-in and no audit trail; they behave like a transferable, revocable secret, and deleting the link removes access for everybody who used it. They cannot be used for files in a Teams shared channel site. People in your organization links require sign-in as a member of the directory, so guests and outsiders cannot use them, but they can still be forwarded inside the organization. Specific people links only work for the named users or security groups, who must authenticate; the link is not transferable and can also be used for people outside the organization. Creating a link does not by itself grant broad access or make the content show up in search or Copilot: Anyone and organization links must first be redeemed by a click, while Specific people links make the item searchable for the listed people. Sending a link from the web interface, Outlook or Teams chat redeems it automatically for up to 100 individual recipients.

sharepoint-subsites.title: Planning your SharePoint hub sites
sharepoint-subsites.notes: This Microsoft Learn guide contrasts the older subsite approach with hub sites. Subsites were used to connect content through nested hierarchy and shared navigation, but a subsite is a physical construct that appears in the URL, so reorganizing the business breaks links. Policy features such as retention and classification apply per site collection, which means enabling one for a subsite often affects the whole collection. The page says subsites leave little room for flexibility and change. Microsoft recommends hub sites going forward: each team or communication site is its own site collection with its own permissions, and a hub models relationships as links rather than ownership, so sites can move between hubs without changing URLs. A hub provides shared navigation and branding, roll-up of news and content, and a shared search scope. A site can belong to only one hub, association does not change permissions, hub navigation can have up to three levels, and hubs can be linked to other hubs up to three levels. Guidance figures include up to 2,000 hub sites per organization and roughly 2,000 sites in a shared search scope. Subsites remain a supported classic feature.

sid-filtering.title: MS-PAC 4.1.2.2 SID Filtering and Claims Transformation
sid-filtering.notes: This protocol specification explains how a domain treats the Privilege Attribute Certificate in a cross-realm ticket-granting ticket. How strictly it filters security identifiers depends on the kind of trust the ticket crossed: member server, within domain, within forest, quarantined within forest, cross-forest, external, quarantined external, or privileged identity management. Each SID falls into an action class. AlwaysFilter SIDs, such as Everyone, Authenticated Users and the built-in domain groups, never cross any boundary. ForestSpecific SIDs, for example well-known RIDs like Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins and Administrator, are removed when they arrive from outside the forest or from a quarantined domain unless they belong to that domain. A special class covers the Enterprise Domain Controllers SID, and a DomainSpecific class covers well-known accounts of the local domain. NeverFilter SIDs always pass. Ordinary user-created identities with RIDs of 1000 or above generally pass external and cross-forest boundaries. Two optional stricter modes drop every SID not belonging to the trusted domain or to the domains listed in the forest trust information.

simple-certificate-enrollment-protocol.title: Simple Certificate Enrollment Protocol (Wikipedia)
simple-certificate-enrollment-protocol.notes: SCEP is a protocol for requesting and issuing digital certificates, described in the informational RFC 8894 and long used as a de facto standard for provisioning network equipment. It was designed by VeriSign for Cisco as a lean alternative to CMC and CMP, aiming to make enrolment simple enough that ordinary users could do it without heavy administrator effort. A requester sends a self-signed PKCS#10 certificate signing request. Authentication is usually done with a shared secret that should be unique per client and single use; it travels in the challengePassword field, and the whole request is protected by an outer encryption layer, which also stops intermediaries such as a registration authority from reading the request. Support for SCEP is widespread: Windows has had it since Windows 2000, Microsoft offers it through the Network Device Enrollment Service and Intune, and Apple devices use it for enterprise PKI. Older versions only support RSA keys, and because PKCS#10 needs signing keys, encryption-only or KEM-only keys cannot be enrolled. Cisco paused its work around 2010 in favour of EST. Peter Gutmann revived the draft in 2015, and RFC 8894 appeared in September 2020 with support for elliptic-curve keys.

smb-signing.title: Control SMB signing behavior (Microsoft Learn)
smb-signing.notes: SMB signing adds a signature to messages on a Server Message Block connection, computed using the session key and cipher suite. The signature contains a hash of the whole message together with the identities of sender and receiver, so a message that is altered in transit no longer matches and the tampering is detected. Microsoft presents this as protection against relay and spoofing attacks. Signing can be required for outbound traffic from the client, for inbound traffic to the server, for both or for neither. Windows 11 version 24H2 Enterprise, Pro and Education require both directions, Windows Server 2025 requires outbound signing, and the Home edition requires neither. Controlling the behavior in full needs Windows 11 24H2 or Windows Server 2025 or later. For the signatures to be effective, Microsoft advises using Kerberos instead of NTLMv2, avoiding connections by IP address and avoiding CNAME aliases. Requiring signing disables guest access, and third-party servers that do not support signing can fail with a STATUS_INVALID_SIGNATURE error; Microsoft does not recommend switching signing off as a workaround. The policy is the client setting Digitally sign communications (always), and the state can be checked with Get-SmbClientConfiguration or Get-SmbServerConfiguration.

socket-io.title: Socket.IO (Wikipedia)
socket-io.notes: Socket.IO is an event-driven JavaScript library for real-time web applications that enables two-way communication between web clients and servers. It consists of a client and a server component with a nearly identical API, and it is also a protocol, so compliant implementations can talk to each other. The main implementation pairs a browser client with a Node.js server, and the article lists further implementations, including an official Deno server and servers written in C++, Java, Python and Swift. It primarily uses the WebSocket protocol and falls back to HTTP long polling when a WebSocket connection cannot be used, while presenting the same interface either way. It can be seen as a wrapper around WebSockets, but it adds features such as heartbeats and timeouts, which a bare WebSocket connection does not provide. The original author is Guillermo Rauch, and Damien Arrachequesne is named as the developer. The project is written in JavaScript, runs cross-platform and is released under the MIT License. The latest stable release shown on the page is 4.7.5 from March 2024. The article offers little history beyond these basics.

software-entropy.title: Software rot and software entropy (Wikipedia)
software-entropy.notes: The article, which Wikipedia files under software rot, describes the decline of a software system's usefulness or performance over time. Software entropy is the narrower idea that repairs and modifications gradually erode a system's structure and raise its complexity. Manny Lehman used the term in 1974 by analogy with the second law of thermodynamics: continuous change increases entropy unless work is done to reduce it. Ivar Jacobson and colleagues argued in 1992 that growing disorder eventually makes a system uneconomical to maintain, and refactoring can postpone that point. Hunt and Thomas used the broken windows metaphor in 1999 to argue for fixing small problems promptly. The page separates dormant rot, where unused software stops working as its environment changes, from active rot, where software under constant modification drifts away from its original design. Causes listed include unanticipated environment changes, latent bugs in rarely used code, side effects of maintenance, outdated libraries, dependence on online services, expiring certificates and deprecated encryption such as TLS 1.0 and 1.1. Remedies are refactoring, hierarchical structure and abstraction, coding conventions, documentation and keeping software updated.

software-extensibility.title: Extensibility (Wikipedia)
software-extensibility.notes: Extensibility is a software engineering and systems design principle that measures how easily a system can be extended and how much effort that takes. Extensions may add or change functionality, and the aim is to do so without breaking what already exists and, ideally, without editing or recompiling the original source. An extensible system keeps its internal structure and data flow largely stable when features arrive. The article ties the idea to agile and iterative development, low coupling, cohesive abstractions and well-defined interfaces, and says extensibility and reusability share traits such as modularity. It distinguishes three forms. White-box extensibility modifies source code, either directly (open-box) or through frameworks that use inheritance and dynamic binding without changing the original (glass-box). Black-box extensibility exposes only interface specifications and relies on configuration tools or scripting languages. Gray-box extensibility offers a specialization interface listing the abstractions that may be refined, plus guidelines. Examples given are device drivers and loadable kernel modules, plug-ins, extension languages, applets and CGI.

software-supply-chain-security.title: Software supply chain (Wikipedia)
software-supply-chain-security.notes: The software supply chain covers the components, libraries, tools and processes used to develop, build and publish a software artifact, including package managers such as PyPI and npm, development tools and cloud services. Because open-source code makes up most of a typical codebase (the article cites a 2022 Linux Foundation figure of 70 to 90 percent), a flaw upstream can reach many downstream users. Examples cited are Heartbleed and Shellshock in 2014, Log4Shell in 2021, the SolarWinds update that more than 18,000 organizations installed in 2020, the Kaseya VSA ransomware attack in 2021 and the XZ Utils backdoor found in 2024. The page frames security around three properties: validity, meaning authenticated contributors and tamper-protected artifacts and build steps; separation, meaning limits on how far a compromise can spread; and transparency, meaning information about components and processes. A software bill of materials inventories every component and helps with vulnerability and licence analysis, and signed provenance attestations record origin, dependencies and build steps. Adoption is uneven: one GitHub study found SBOMs in only about 0.56 percent of popular repositories. Executive Order 14028 of May 2021 directed NIST and NTIA to issue SBOM guidance.

spec-driven-development.title: Spec-driven development with AI: get started with a new open source toolkit (GitHub Blog)
spec-driven-development.notes: GitHub describes spec-driven development as starting from a written specification instead of code. The spec acts as a contract for behavior and as the source of truth that AI coding agents use to generate, test and validate code. The article argues that the weakness in AI coding is less the agent than how people prompt it: models are good at completing patterns but cannot infer unstated requirements, so a vague request forces guessing and errors show up late. GitHub released an open-source toolkit called Spec Kit, which works with GitHub Copilot, Claude Code and Gemini CLI and is driven by a specify command-line tool plus the specify, plan and tasks commands. The workflow has four phases with a checkpoint after each. In Specify the developer states what and why and the agent expands it into user journeys and success criteria without a tech stack. In Plan the developer adds stack, architecture and constraints and the agent drafts a technical plan. In Tasks the agent splits the plan into small, reviewable pieces. In Implement the agent works through them while the developer reviews focused changes. The suggested uses are new projects, features in existing code and legacy modernization.

spf.title: Sender Policy Framework (Wikipedia)
spf.notes: SPF is an email authentication method that lets a domain publish, in a DNS TXT record, which hosts and IP addresses may send mail for it. A receiving server checks the SMTP envelope-from address (the Return-Path), not the visible From header, so DMARC is needed to tie the result to the From address. A record starts with v=spf1, followed by mechanisms such as ip4, ip6, a, mx and include, each with a qualifier: plus for pass, question mark for neutral, tilde for softfail and minus for fail, with all usually at the end. Modifiers include redirect and exp. Evaluation may trigger at most ten DNS-querying mechanisms, and exceeding that limit, or more than two void lookups, must produce a permanent error. A known drawback is that plain forwarding breaks SPF unless the forwarder rewrites the return path, for example with a Sender Rewriting Scheme. Domains that send no mail should publish v=spf1 -all, and publishers are advised to test with softfail before enforcing fail. The specification is RFC 7208 from April 2014, which replaced the experimental RFC 4408 of 2006, and the dedicated SPF DNS record type was discontinued in favour of TXT. Since February 2024 Gmail has required SPF, DKIM and DMARC from bulk senders.

sql-join.title: Join (SQL) (Wikipedia)
sql-join.notes: A join combines columns from two or more tables into a new result, matching rows on related fields, and corresponds to the join operation of relational algebra. The article covers the main variants. A cross join returns the Cartesian product, pairing every row of one table with every row of the other. An inner join keeps only pairs whose join predicate is satisfied, so rows without a match, for example an employee without a department, are dropped, which can silently lose data if join columns may be NULL. Outer joins keep unmatched rows and fill the missing side with NULLs: a left outer join keeps all rows of the left table, a right outer join keeps all of the right, and a full outer join keeps both. Equi-joins use only equality comparisons, other operators make a theta join, USING is shorthand for same-named columns, and a natural join joins on all identically named columns, which most experts discourage. A self-join joins a table to itself using aliases. NULL never matches any value, including another NULL. Because inner joins are commutative and associative, the optimizer may choose the order and algorithm, typically nested loop, sort-merge or hash join.

sql.title: SQL (Wikipedia)
sql.notes: SQL, Structured Query Language, is a domain-specific language for managing data in relational database management systems. It is largely declarative: a statement says what data is wanted rather than how to reach it, which was an advantage over older record-access APIs such as ISAM and VSAM. Statements fall informally into query, definition, control and manipulation sublanguages, and cover querying, inserting, updating and deleting rows, defining schemas and controlling access. It was developed at IBM in the early 1970s by Donald Chamberlin and Raymond Boyce after Edgar Codd's relational model, first under the name SEQUEL for the System R prototype, shortened to SQL because of a trademark. Oracle shipped one of the first commercial implementations in 1979. ANSI adopted SQL in 1986 and ISO in 1987, and the standard, ISO/IEC 9075, has been revised repeatedly, for example adding recursive queries and triggers in SQL:1999, window functions and XML in SQL:2003, JSON operations in SQL:2016 and a native JSON type and property graph queries in SQL:2023. Real products deviate from the standard in date handling, string concatenation, NULL treatment and case sensitivity, so portability is limited. Critics point to duplicate rows and NULL semantics as departures from relational theory.

sqlbi.title: About SQLBI
sqlbi.notes: SQLBI presents itself as a small team of Business Intelligence specialists who work mainly with Microsoft technologies: Analysis Services, Power Pivot and Power BI. The About page names Marco Russo and Alberto Ferrari as consultants and mentors and Daniele Perilli as creative designer. The company says it has taught hundreds of classroom courses in many countries and offers recorded video courses on DAX, SSAS, data modeling and data presentation, plus custom training and mentoring. Consulting services include remote consulting for quick expert help and architectural reviews. The team has published books, mostly through Microsoft Press, including The Definitive Guide to DAX, Optimizing DAX and DAX Patterns. The sqlbi.com website was launched in 2004 and publishes in-depth articles, free tools and videos. Related projects listed are DAX Guide, a DAX language reference from 2018; DAX.do, an online playground for DAX queries; DAX Patterns; DAX Formatter; Bravo for Power BI, a desktop companion tool; DAX Optimizer, a service for tuning models and reports; DAX Lib, a library of reusable snippets; and OKVIZ, a source of Power BI visuals. The page also notes Microsoft partner status and regular conference speaking.

strangler-fig-pattern.title: Strangler Fig pattern (Azure Architecture Center)
strangler-fig-pattern.notes: The Strangler Fig pattern migrates a legacy system step by step. Individual functions are replaced by new applications or services until the new system covers everything and the legacy system can be switched off, while clients keep using the same interface and do not notice the migration. A facade, which is a proxy placed in front of the back end, intercepts requests and routes each to either the legacy application or the new services. The migration has four phases: introduce the facade, shift functionality incrementally so that more traffic goes to the new side, decommission the legacy system once nothing depends on it, and finally remove the facade so clients talk to the new system directly. The article recommends it when replacing a large system at once would be risky and the old system can keep running for a long time. It advises against it when requests cannot be intercepted, when the legacy code and integration points cannot be changed, when the system is small, or when quick decommissioning is required. Considerations include shared data stores, keeping the facade from becoming a bottleneck or single point of failure, and using an anti-corruption layer between old and new. A database example extracts one domain at a time using change data capture.

streamable-http.title: Model Context Protocol specification: Transports (2025-06-18)
streamable-http.notes: The Model Context Protocol encodes messages as JSON-RPC and defines two standard transports, stdio and Streamable HTTP. Streamable HTTP replaces the HTTP+SSE transport of protocol version 2024-11-05. The server is an independent process that offers one HTTP endpoint path, the MCP endpoint, supporting both POST and GET. Every client message is a new POST request, and the client must accept both JSON and event-stream responses. For a request, the server answers either with a single JSON object or by opening a Server-Sent Events stream that can carry related server messages before the final response; notifications and responses from the client get a 202 Accepted. The client may also issue a GET to open a stream for server-initiated messages. Servers may attach event IDs so a client can resume after a broken connection by sending the Last-Event-ID header. An optional session is created by returning an Mcp-Session-Id header at initialization, which the client must then send on all later requests; an expired session yields a 404, and the client can end it with DELETE. Clients also send an MCP-Protocol-Version header. For security, servers must validate the Origin header against DNS rebinding, should bind to localhost when running locally and should authenticate connections.

subnet-mask.title: Subnet (Wikipedia)
subnet-mask.notes: An IP address has two logical parts, a network prefix used for routing and a host identifier, and all hosts in one subnet share the same prefix in the most significant bits. In IPv4 the subnet mask is a 32-bit bitmask written in dotted decimal that consists of a run of ones followed by a run of zeros; the ones mark the network prefix and the zeros the host bits. Applying the mask to an address with a bitwise AND yields the network prefix, for example 255.255.255.0 for a /24 prefix. CIDR notation writes the first address, a slash and the prefix length, such as 198.51.100.0/24, and is the standard form for both IPv4 and IPv6. Subnetting moves high-order host bits into the prefix to create smaller subnets: borrowing two bits from a /24 yields four /26 subnets with mask 255.255.255.192, each with 62 usable hosts. A subnet with h host bits has 2 to the power h minus 2 usable addresses because the network and broadcast addresses are reserved, with /31 point-to-point links as an exception. A router compares source, mask and destination to decide whether a destination is local. Before CIDR, classful networking implied the prefix length from the leading bits. IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses with /64 as the usual subnet size and has no broadcast.

suggestion-acceptance-rate.title: About Copilot usage metrics (GitHub Docs)
suggestion-acceptance-rate.notes: GitHub's documentation on Copilot usage metrics treats acceptance rate as one of several adoption signals. It says the metric measures how often developers accept Copilot's suggestions, with inline suggestions as the example, and that a high rate suggests the suggestions are relevant and useful. The page does not publish a formula, so numerator and denominator are not specified. It advises reading the rate together with other indicators instead of in isolation: for instance, steady daily active users combined with a rising acceptance rate points to growing trust and value. The metrics themselves come from usage metrics APIs at enterprise, organization, repository and user level, a dashboard with 28-day trends, a code generation dashboard, an impact dashboard that groups users into adoption cohorts, and an NDJSON export for BI tools. Most data comes from IDE telemetry, so telemetry must be enabled and reach GitHub; Copilot Chat on GitHub.com and GitHub Mobile are excluded. Data appears within two full UTC days, enterprise reports deduplicate users across organizations while organization reports do not, and lines-of-code figures are described as a directional view of output rather than precise measures.

supervisor-worker-pattern.title: Build a personal assistant with subagents: the supervisor pattern (LangChain docs)
supervisor-worker-pattern.notes: The LangChain tutorial describes the supervisor pattern as a central supervisor agent coordinating specialised worker agents, each with its own tools and prompt, where the supervisor decides which worker handles each part of a request. In the example, a calendar agent and an email agent are each wrapped as a high-level tool that takes a natural-language request and returns only the worker's final message, so the supervisor never sees the intermediate tool calls and only routes at domain level and combines results. Reasons to use it are that splitting tools across workers avoids overloading one agent with many similar tools, which can hurt performance; prompts and tools can be improved and tested per worker; new domains can be added without touching existing ones; and the workflow is centrally controlled. Calls are sequential by default, and parallel tool calls in one model response run in parallel. Human review can be added through middleware on sensitive tools, with a checkpointer on the supervisor. Trade-offs are an extra model call per wrapper, information loss if a worker's final message omits details, no direct conversation between workers and users, and needless overhead when only a few tools exist.

systems-engineering.title: Systems engineering (Wikipedia)
systems-engineering.notes: Systems engineering is an interdisciplinary field that designs, integrates and manages complex systems across their life cycle, applying systems thinking and drawing on mechanical, electrical, software, industrial and civil engineering as well as project management. Definitions of a system vary between standards, but they share the view of interacting elements organized for a purpose. The term goes back to Bell Telephone Laboratories in the 1940s, when it became clear that a system's overall properties can differ greatly from the sum of its parts, and INCOSE was founded in 1990 as NCOSE and renamed in 1995. Work is organised in a technical process and a management process, using life-cycle models such as waterfall and the V model with feedback between stages. Key concepts include complexity, holism and emergent behavior, early requirements elicitation, trade studies with methods such as Pugh or QFD, interface design, modeling and simulation, graphical notations such as SysML and configuration management. Reliability, availability and maintainability are handled with tools such as FMEA and fault tree analysis, and risk and safety engineering are part of the process.

t-shaped-skills.title: T-shaped skills (Wikipedia)
t-shaped-skills.notes: T-shaped skills is a metaphor from recruitment for the abilities of a worker. The vertical bar of the letter stands for deep expertise in one field, and the horizontal bar stands for the ability to collaborate with experts in other disciplines and to apply knowledge outside one's own specialty. The earliest popular reference given is David Guest in 1995, and IDEO chief executive Tim Brown backed the idea as a way to screen resumes and build interdisciplinary teams for creative work. Earlier uses are cited as well, including a 1978 article by D. L. Johnston titled Scientists Become Managers: The T-Shaped Man, and McKinsey's internal use of the phrase in the 1980s for recruiting and developing consultants. The term is common in agile software development, where it describes cross-skilled developers and testers who can work across a Scrum team. The article lists variants: X-shaped for leadership, I-shaped for depth without communication skills, tree-shaped for depth across many branches, Gamma and M shapes from research on data science communities, pi-shaped for broad management skill over several deep specialties, and V-shaped from convergence research where two disciplines meet at a shared problem.

teams-auto-attendant.title: Set up an auto attendant (Microsoft Teams)
teams-auto-attendant.notes: An auto attendant is a Teams Phone component that answers inbound calls, plays greetings and menus, and routes callers to people, call queues, voice apps, resource accounts, external numbers, voicemail or announcements. Admins create one in the Teams admin center under Voice, either with a quick setup for simple routing or an advanced eight-step wizard, or with PowerShell. The advanced flow covers general information (name, language, voice inputs, operator), call handling hours (default 09:00 to 17:00 every day), separate business-hours and after-hours call flows, optional holiday call flows, a dial scope that decides who appears in dial by name and dial by extension, and optional authorized users. Greetings can be uploaded audio or typed text of up to 1,000 characters read by text-to-speech. Menus map keys 0 to 9, star and pound to destinations, optionally with voice commands. An operator is recommended as a fallback, and dial keys conflict with directory search, so directory search should be set to none when keys are assigned. The language list has 54 locales, and where speech recognition is missing, voice inputs are disabled. New users can take up to 36 hours to appear in the directory. Destination users must be voice enabled through Teams add-on licensing.

teams-meeting-transcription.title: Transcription and captions in Teams meetings and events (Microsoft Learn)
teams-meeting-transcription.notes: Transcription creates a written record of what is said in a Teams meeting or event, with timestamps and speaker attribution, that participants can read afterwards. It is separate from live captions, which show subtitles during the meeting and are not saved. Transcription is controlled per organizer and per user: the organizer must have it enabled for the meeting, and so must the person who starts the recording or transcript. Administrators set it in meeting policies or events policies in the Teams admin center or with PowerShell, using AllowTranscription for meetings and TranscriptionForWebinar or TranscriptionForTownhall for events; it is on by default in new meeting policies. Transcripts are stored with the meeting recordings in OneDrive and SharePoint, and the link can break if the video is copied within the same site. More than 70 locales are supported. Teams Premium adds live translated transcription and more caption languages. Organizers can stop participants from copying or forwarding chat, captions, transcripts and AI recap content, which is on by default. If the organizer turns off Copilot in Teams meetings and events, recording and transcription are turned off too.

teams-personal-tabs.title: Tabs in Microsoft Teams apps (Microsoft Learn)
teams-personal-tabs.notes: Tabs are client-aware web pages embedded in Microsoft Teams, Outlook and Microsoft 365; technically they are iframes pointing to domains declared in the app manifest. There are static and configurable tabs, usable in personal, group chat and channel scopes. Personal tabs are static tabs that belong to a personal app scoped to a single user and are pinned in the left navigation bar. The page lists personal tabs among the static tab scopes, and static tabs can now also be extended to group chats, channels and meetings, where only one tab per app can be pinned. A static tab's content URL is set in the contentUrl property of the staticTabs array in the manifest, and the content is the same for every user. An app may declare up to 16 static tabs. The page must include the Teams JavaScript client library and call app initialize after loading, and it receives context such as user, locale, theme and entity ID. Features include Microsoft Entra ID awareness, single sign-on, deep linking and dialogs. Because tabs run in sandboxed iframes, native plugins are not available. Tabs can be built with the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit.

temporary-access-pass.title: Configure a Temporary Access Pass in Microsoft Entra ID
temporary-access-pass.notes: A Temporary Access Pass is a time-limited passcode that lets a user sign in to Microsoft Entra ID, typically to register passwordless methods such as passkeys (FIDO2), Windows Hello for Business or passwordless phone sign-in, or to recover access after losing a strong method. It does not replace the password. The tenant policy under Authentication methods controls who may use it and sets the minimum lifetime (default 1 hour), maximum lifetime (default 8 hours), default lifetime (1 hour), whether passes are single use, and the passcode length (default 8, allowed 8 to 48 characters); lifetimes may range from 10 minutes to 43,200 minutes, which is 30 days. An Authentication Administrator is the minimum role to create one, and the passcode is shown only once. Each user can have only one pass, and a new one overrides an existing one. Only members and internal guests can receive it, not external guests. With a one-time pass, passwordless registration must be completed within 10 minutes of sign-in. Expiry does not end existing sessions, so Conditional Access sign-in frequency can limit that. It is not supported with the NPS extension or the AD FS adapter.

tensorrt.title: TensorRT (Wikipedia)
tensorrt.notes: TensorRT is Nvidia's software development kit and runtime for optimizing trained deep learning models for inference on Nvidia GPUs, part of Nvidia's deep learning software stack since 2017. It imports models from frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow and ONNX and compiles them into optimized engines aimed at low latency and high throughput. The core is a C++ library with C++ and Python APIs; models can be described through the network definition API or imported with the ONNX parser, and engines can be built through the APIs or with the trtexec command-line tool. Optimizations happen at graph and kernel level, including layer fusion and choosing efficient implementations, and it supports dynamic shapes and specific optimizations for transformer and large language model workloads. Supported precisions include FP32, FP16, BF16, FP8 and INT8. A plugin mechanism covers custom or unsupported layers, and companion tools include Polygraphy for debugging and ONNX-GraphSurgeon for editing ONNX graphs. The family also includes TensorRT-LLM, an open-source toolkit for serving large language models, and TensorRT-RTX for consumer RTX GPUs. It runs on Linux and Windows. The packaged SDK is proprietary, while the public repositories on GitHub use Apache 2.0.

terraform-provider.title: Providers (Terraform language documentation)
terraform-provider.notes: Terraform relies on plugins called providers to interact with cloud platforms, SaaS products and other APIs. A provider supplies resource types and data sources, so every resource Terraform manages comes from some provider, and without one Terraform cannot manage infrastructure. Most providers target an infrastructure platform, though some offer local utilities such as random value generation. A configuration declares the providers it needs so Terraform can install them, and a provider block can carry settings like regions or endpoints. Providers are released separately from Terraform with their own versions, and the main public directory is the Terraform Registry. For production, versions should be constrained in the required providers block, and a dependency lock file created by the CLI should be committed to pin exact versions. The CLI installs providers during terraform init from a registry, a local mirror or a cache, while HCP Terraform and Terraform Enterprise install them on every run. Registry badges describe tiers: Official (maintained by HashiCorp), Partner Premier, Partner, Community and Archived. Providers are written in Go with the Terraform Plugin SDK. Providers outside the hosted registries may need extra credentials supplied through a netrc file.

thin-client.title: Thin client (Wikipedia)
thin-client.notes: A thin client is a simple, low-performance computer built to connect to a remote desktop or computing environment on a server. Most of the work, such as running applications, computing and storing data, happens on the server, whereas a traditional PC does it locally. Thin clients usually belong to an infrastructure based on application virtualization, hosted shared desktops or virtual desktop infrastructure. Hardware is typically low-energy with flash storage and no moving parts, and the software is a minimal interface with remote access agents such as RDP, ICA or PCoIP on a lightweight, often read-only operating system. The article lists advantages: low cost of ownership, easy replacement, central deployment of updates, and better security because little data is stored locally. Drawbacks include server infrastructure that can cancel the savings, limited support for local peripherals, dependence on network bandwidth, servers as a possible single point of failure, and difficulty with graphics-heavy work without GPUs on the host. A zero client is the simplest form. Historically, thin clients trace back to mainframe terminals and X terminals, and Citrix WinFrame in 1995 led to Windows Remote Desktop Services. The term was coined by Tim Negris of Oracle in 1993.

three-way-matching.title: Three-way matching policies (Dynamics 365 Finance)
three-way-matching.notes: The page explains invoice matching in Dynamics 365 Finance through worked examples. In two-way matching, invoice lines are matched to purchase order lines on price. In three-way matching, invoice lines are matched to purchase order lines on price and also to product receipt lines on quantity, so the invoiced quantity must equal what was received. The matching policy can be set at the legal entity level, per item, per item and vendor combination, and overridden on an individual purchase order line, which allows a stricter policy for a specific order. Tolerances apply to price: the net unit price tolerance is a percentage, and the price totals tolerance, set through the Match price totals field of the legal entity, can be a percentage, an amount or both. No quantity tolerance is shown for three-way items. In the examples an invoice at 8,100 against a purchase price of 8,000 passes within an 8 percent tolerance, while an invoice of 41.00 against 40.00 fails a 2 percent tolerance, and a line fails the quantity check if no product receipt has been posted yet. Warning icons mark failed checks on the invoice line. If approval is required, the Approve posting with matching discrepancies toggle on the Invoice matching details page must be set before posting.

toil.title: Eliminating Toil (Google SRE Book)
toil.notes: Google's Site Reliability Engineering book defines toil as operational work tied to running a production service that is manual, repetitive, automatable, tactical and interrupt-driven, brings no lasting value, and grows in step with service size, traffic or user count. Not every toil task has all of these traits, and the more it has, the more likely it is toil. Overhead such as meetings or training is not toil, and neither is grungy work that leaves a permanent improvement. Novel work is not toil, and work needing human judgment becomes toil if the judgment is needed repeatedly because a system is poorly designed. The goal is to keep toil below 50 percent of each SRE's time, measured over several quarters, with at least half spent on engineering. On-call sets a floor, around a third in a six-person rotation, and Google's surveys found an average of about 33 percent, ranging from 0 to 80 percent for individuals. The largest sources were interrupts, on-call response and releases. The chapter warns that excess toil causes career stagnation, low morale, slower progress, attrition and role confusion, and that toil expands to fill available time. Remedies are automating repetitive tasks and redesigning systems so failures need no manual response.

transactional-outbox-pattern.title: Pattern: Transactional outbox (microservices.io)
transactional-outbox-pattern.notes: The pattern addresses a common problem: a service must update its database and also publish a message or event to a broker, and the two actions must be atomic. Two-phase commit is often unavailable or undesirable, and without it a message sent before commit may be wrong if the transaction rolls back, while one sent after commit can be lost if the service crashes. Messages must also keep the order in which the service produced them. The solution is to store each outgoing message in an outbox, in the same database transaction that changes the business data. The page names four participants: the sender service, the database, the message outbox (a table in a relational database, or a property on each record in a NoSQL store) and a message relay that reads the outbox and forwards messages to the broker. The relay can be implemented by transaction log tailing or by a polling publisher. Benefits are that no two-phase commit is needed, messages are sent if and only if the transaction commits, and order is preserved. Drawbacks are that it is error prone because a developer may forget to write the message, and that the relay may publish duplicates, so consumers must be idempotent, for example by tracking processed message IDs.

triple-peak-workday.title: Breaking down the infinite workday (Microsoft Work Trend Index)
triple-peak-workday.notes: Microsoft's Work Trend Index report on the infinite workday says the triple peak day began during the pandemic and is now the norm for many workers rather than a passing trend. Activity peaks in the morning and afternoon and then again in the evening, and the report treats this as part of a workday that keeps stretching. It does not give a formal definition of the pattern, but it offers data: meetings after 8 pm are up 16 percent year over year, the average employee sends or receives more than 50 messages outside core hours, and by 10 pm 29 percent of active workers are back in their inboxes. A related Microsoft Research study found remote developers often treat evenings as a quiet, productive window while hybrid workers more often find those hours stressful. Other findings are that 40 percent of people online at 6 am are checking email, the average worker gets 117 emails and 153 Teams messages a day, and a meeting, email or notification interrupts employees about every two minutes. The telemetry covers Microsoft 365 data to February 15, 2025, and the survey reached 31,000 knowledge workers in 31 markets. The report recommends managers set clearer expectations and use AI agents for low-value tasks.

truesec.title: Truesec: cybersecurity company (company website)
truesec.notes: According to its own website, Truesec is a cybersecurity company headquartered in Stockholm, Sweden, and part of the Truesec Group. Its services fall into managed services, digital forensics and incident response, consulting, and solutions. Managed services include managed detection and response for IT and OT environments, managed threat exposure and managed identity security. Incident response covers response exercises, preparedness planning and retainers. Consulting spans offensive security, application security, governance and risk advisory, cloud, infrastructure and network, AI and data security, identity and intelligence services. Solutions listed include OT security, secure AI adoption, supply chain security, zero trust and embedded systems and hardware security. The company says it works with Microsoft, CrowdStrike and other security vendors and serves enterprises, small and medium businesses and public sector bodies. It reports more than 400 cybersecurity staff, over 40 full-time incident response experts handling more than 200 breaches a year, and claims the largest security operations center in the Nordic region, which are company claims. Listed offices are in Stockholm and Malmo in Sweden, Copenhagen and Aarhus in Denmark, Espoo in Finland and Munich in Germany.

unified-tenant-configuration-management.title: Tenant Configuration Management APIs in Microsoft Graph (overview)
unified-tenant-configuration-management.notes: The Tenant Configuration Management APIs in Microsoft Graph let administrators control and manage configuration settings for an organization, within a single workload or across several. Administrators describe the desired state declaratively: a declaration covers one or more resources and each resource has one or more properties. The page explains that in the traditional model every administrator works with their own credentials on whatever they can reach, so nobody has full control of the tenant configuration and drift from the intended state is hard to see, with teams detecting and fixing it by hand in a slow and error-prone way. Two capabilities address this. The configurationMonitor APIs automate monitoring of tenant settings and flag deviations from the desired state, which is drift detection. The configurationSnapshotJob APIs retrieve the current configuration across workloads as a declarative view that helps audits, reviews and troubleshooting. Supported workloads include Microsoft Defender, Entra, Exchange Online, Intune, Purview and Teams. Authentication requires setting up a Tenant Configuration Management service principal. The overview page does not state preview status, specific permission scopes or limits.

user-defined-routes.title: Azure virtual network traffic routing (user-defined routes)
user-defined-routes.notes: Azure builds a route table for each subnet that holds system routes, such as virtual network, internet and none, plus optional routes for peering, gateways and service endpoints. Custom routes override them and come from two sources: user-defined routes (UDRs), which are static routes created in a route table, and BGP routes exchanged with an on-premises gateway. A route table can be associated with zero or more subnets, but each subnet has at most one, and a table holds up to 400 UDRs by default, or up to 1,000 with Azure Virtual Network Manager routing configuration. Allowed next hop types are virtual appliance, virtual network gateway (only a VPN gateway), virtual network, internet and none; peering and service endpoints cannot be chosen. A virtual appliance needs a next hop IP, IP forwarding enabled and direct connectivity, and should sit in a different subnet from the resources it serves. When routes overlap, the longest prefix match wins, and for the same prefix a UDR beats BGP, which beats system routes. Routes using service tags are limited to 25 per table. Overriding 0.0.0.0/0 sends all traffic to the next hop, and such a table must not be associated with the GatewaySubnet of a VPN gateway.

user-experience-design.title: User experience design (Wikipedia)
user-experience-design.notes: User experience design covers the whole experience a person has with a company, its services and its products. It is user-centered and relies on research, data and testing rather than aesthetic preference, and it is broader than user interface design, taking in usability, usefulness, desirability, brand perception and performance as part of the wider customer experience. The field grew out of human factors and ergonomics, and the term gained ground in the early 1990s, with Don Norman credited for coining and popularizing it because human interface and usability were too narrow. Core elements are user research (interviews, surveys, field studies), user modeling with personas, interaction design, visual design and information architecture. The process starts with research and models, moves to wireframes that define layout, flow and behavior, then to pixel-level screens built with developers, and continues with usability and A/B testing and refinement, ideally early and often. Typical deliverables are wireframes, prototypes, user flows, mockups and specification documents. Usability is treated as a subset of UX: good usability is essential but does not guarantee a good experience.

vba.title: Visual Basic for Applications (Wikipedia)
vba.notes: VBA is Microsoft's event-driven programming language built into most desktop Microsoft Office applications, derived from pre-.NET Visual Basic. It is used to write user-defined functions, automate tasks in a host application, call the Windows API through DLLs, customize menus, toolbars and UserForms, and control one application from another through OLE Automation. Code is compiled to a proprietary intermediate language called P-Code, stored inside the document file and run by a virtual machine in the host, so VBA normally cannot run as a standalone program. Excel 5.0 in 1993 was the first Microsoft application to include it, and version 7.0 in 2010 added 64-bit support. Microsoft stopped offering VBA licences to new customers in 2007. Hosts include Access, Excel, Word, Outlook, PowerPoint, Project and Visio, and several third-party products such as AutoCAD and LibreOffice. VBA is not compatible with VB.NET and apart from its COM interface is proprietary. Macros can carry malware, so security depends on user settings, and in February 2022 Microsoft announced that macros in files downloaded from the internet would be blocked by default. Alternatives mentioned include VSTO, VSTA and Microsoft Power Fx.

vendor-posting-profile.title: Vendor posting profiles (Dynamics 365 Finance)
vendor-posting-profile.notes: Vendor posting profiles control how vendor transactions are posted to the general ledger. Each profile assigns ledger accounts and document settings to all vendors, a vendor group or a single vendor, and applies to purchase orders, vendor invoices and cash payments. The system picks the most specific match: first a profile for the specific vendor account (account code Table), then one for the vendor group, then the one for all vendors. A default profile is set on the Ledger and Sales Tax FastTab of the Accounts payable parameters page and appears in new document headers, where it can be changed. Setup fields include the profile code, description, account code, the vendor or group, and the summary account, which is the ledger account used for the vendors in the profile; if posting definitions are enabled on the General ledger parameters page, the transaction posting definition for vendor invoices is used instead. Further fields cover the settle account for cash flow forecasts, the sales tax prepayment account, an Arrival account that holds unapproved invoices from the invoice register journal, and an offset account for those postings.

vibe-engineering.title: Vibe engineering (Simon Willison, 7 October 2025)
vibe-engineering.notes: Simon Willison proposed the term vibe engineering in October 2025 for a disciplined way of building software with AI, set against vibe coding. Vibe coding is fast, loose and prompt-driven, with little attention to how the code works. Vibe engineering, as he describes it, is what experienced professionals do when they speed up their work with LLMs and coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex CLI and Gemini CLI while staying accountable for the software they ship. He notes that some engineers run several agents in parallel, which he finds effective but mentally exhausting. The article lists practices that agents reward: automated tests, planning and iterating on a plan before implementation, good documentation, version control, CI, linting and preview deployments, a code review culture, management skills for giving clear instructions, strong manual QA, research skills and judgment about what to delegate to AI. His conclusion is that these tools amplify existing expertise and demand working at the top of your game on architecture, specifications, success criteria and agentic loop design. An update dated February 2026 says agentic engineering is emerging as the preferred term.

virtual-private-network.title: Virtual private network (Wikipedia)
virtual-private-network.notes: A VPN is an overlay network that extends a private network across a public one such as the internet, using tunneling protocols and encryption to carry traffic between hosts. The article describes several configurations: host-to-network remote access, where an individual computer opens a tunnel into an office network; site-to-site, where gateways connect whole networks; provider-provisioned VPNs run by carriers; and consumer VPN services. Encryption protects confidentiality, but a VPN does not make a user anonymous, since the provider and the visited services may still see activity. Split tunneling lets a user reach the private network through the tunnel while using the open internet directly, which saves bandwidth but can cause DNS leaks and bypass gateway security. Traditional VPNs are point-to-point and generally do not carry broadcast traffic. Protocols covered are IPsec with IKEv1 and IKEv2, L2TP, SSL/TLS-based options such as OpenVPN, Microsoft's SSTP, DTLS and WireGuard, which uses Curve25519 and ChaCha20-Poly1305 and entered the Linux kernel in 2020. MPLS-based trusted VPNs rely on a single provider's network rather than cryptography. Mobile VPNs keep sessions alive when the endpoint address changes.

virtual-table-data-provider.title: Get started with virtual tables (entities) in Dataverse
virtual-table-data-provider.notes: Virtual tables, also called virtual entities, let Dataverse show data from external systems as tables without copying it; records are retrieved from the source at runtime. A virtual table is defined like a custom table but has no physical table in the Dataverse database. Each one is tied to a virtual table data provider and optionally to a data source that carries connection information. The provider is the component that translates Dataverse requests into calls to the external system. The OData v4 provider is included and installed by default and supports create, retrieve, retrieve multiple, update and delete; an Azure Cosmos DB provider is available from the marketplace; and for other sources developers can write a custom provider by implementing plug-ins for each operation and registering them with the Plug-in Registration tool, with full CRUD now supported. Tables and columns must be mapped to the external data, and the provider has to supply a GUID that identifies each external record. Limits include support for organization-owned tables only, no field-level security, no auditing, no search, no charts or dashboards, no calculated or rollup columns, no offline caching, and no conversion between virtual and standard tables.

voucher.title: Ledger and subledger (Dynamics 365 Finance)
voucher.notes: Microsoft Learn describes the voucher as the shared reference that connects a subledger document to its accounting entries in the ledger. The chain works like this: a source document such as a customer invoice or product receipt is posted in a module like Accounts receivable, Accounts payable or Inventory. Posting profiles then create subledger journal account entries, using main accounts from the chart of accounts and the document's financial dimensions, as a balanced set of debits and credits; for example a 100 dollar product receipt debits Inventory and credits Purchase accrual. These entries are transferred to the general ledger either in detail or summarized, depending on the General ledger parameters, so the subledger can show more entries than the ledger. The voucher ties the ledger postings back to the originating document. For traceability, a user can open the product receipt journal and choose Vouchers to see the ledger entry, or go from General ledger to Inquiries and reports, Voucher transactions, and use the View subledger journal tab to see the detail behind a voucher. The article does not explain voucher numbering or assignment rules.

who-knows-whom.title: Who knows whom (Dynamics 365 Sales)
who-knows-whom.notes: Who knows whom is a Dynamics 365 Sales feature that helps sellers find colleagues able to introduce them to a lead or contact. It analyzes communication patterns in emails and meetings, suggests colleagues who have interacted with the lead or contact, and lets the seller request an introduction by email. Two data sources exist. Basic information uses email and meeting data in Dynamics 365, is available out of the box in all regions and needs no setup. Enhanced information uses Exchange data, requires an administrator to configure server-side synchronization and is supported only for certain Dynamics 365 Sales licenses. The widget shows up to five people in the organization who have communicated with the lead or contact through calls and emails, with the strength of each connection, in a graph or list view. It appears on the Sales Insights form and on the main Contact and Lead forms. To get an introduction, the seller opens a lead or contact in the Sales Hub app, picks a colleague based on connection strength, selects Get introduced, which appears only when server-side synchronization is set up, and edits and sends the template email. If an insufficient privileges message appears, the admin must grant access.

windows-enterprise-multi-session.title: Windows Enterprise multi-session FAQ (Azure Virtual Desktop)
windows-enterprise-multi-session.notes: Windows 10 Enterprise multi-session and Windows 11 Enterprise multi-session allow several users to hold interactive sessions on one virtual machine at the same time, which previously only Windows Server offered. It is a virtual edition of Windows Enterprise intended for pooled host pools in Azure Virtual Desktop, and users get a familiar Windows client experience. The page gives no fixed per-VM user limit; capacity depends on vCPU, memory, disk and vGPU resources and on user workloads, so Microsoft advises testing. It uses per-user Windows licensing instead of RDS client access licenses, and production use outside Azure Virtual Desktop is not allowed under the licence. The operating system reports ProductType 3 like Windows Server, so remote desktop session host tooling works, although some installers that check for a client product type may refuse to run. It does not activate against an on-premises KMS server, Remote Desktop IP Virtualization is unsupported, existing Pro or Enterprise VMs cannot be converted to multi-session, and in-place OS upgrades of pooled session hosts are unsupported. FSLogix is preinstalled and free for Azure Virtual Desktop users, though the profile container must still be configured.

workstream.title: Create workstreams (Dynamics 365 Customer Service)
workstream.notes: A workstream is a container that enriches, routes and assigns work items in Dynamics 365 Customer Service, and each one is tied to a channel such as live chat, voice or case. There are three types: messaging, which routes live chat, SMS, social and Teams conversations; record, which routes records such as cases, emails and activities and needs unified routing; and voice, which routes calls and supports push mode only. Workstreams are created in the Copilot Service admin center under Customer support, Workstreams. When creating one, the admin chooses a name, type, channel and a fallback queue, and a work distribution mode of push or pick, which cannot be edited later. Routing consists of work classification rules and route-to-queue rules, with the fallback queue used when no rule matches. Work distribution settings cover auto-close after inactivity, capacity that is unit based or profile based, how long capacity is blocked for wrap-up, allowed presences, the default skill matching algorithm (exact match, closest match or none) and whether the same representative keeps the whole conversation. Bots such as Copilot Studio agents can be added, but only in push-based workstreams. A workstream can be copied, shared or deleted after removing its dependencies.

wortell.title: Wortell (company website)
wortell.notes: Wortell is a Dutch IT services company with its head office in Lijnden, and the website has English and Belgian versions. The meta description puts its size at about 250 colleagues, and the company calls itself the number one Microsoft partner in the Netherlands, with the mission statement We empower people. Its offering is grouped into three areas. AI Business Solutions covers Copilot, predictive models, intelligent automation, Copilot adoption and change management, agent governance and a managed AI and analytics service called Wortell MAIA. Cloud and AI Platforms covers Azure platforms, data architecture, migrations, Power Platform and on-location specialists through Wortell Onsite. Security covers round-the-clock managed detection and response, Microsoft Sentinel, Zero Trust, dark web monitoring, incident response, penetration testing and red teaming, attack surface management, managed data security and security awareness. Services are framed as moving from vision to value, with envisioning, a service model and managed services, and there are learning offerings including in-company training. Listed recognition includes Microsoft Security Excellence Awards and Microsoft partner of the year titles for the Netherlands.

wpf.title: Windows Presentation Foundation overview (Microsoft Learn)
wpf.notes: WPF is a UI framework for Windows desktop applications, described as resolution independent with a vector-based rendering engine that uses graphics hardware. It exists in two implementations: the open-source version on modern .NET, hosted on GitHub and running on Windows only, and the older .NET Framework 4 version, which is an operating system component. Microsoft recommends moving to .NET for performance and new APIs. The programming model follows normal .NET patterns and adds dependency properties and routed events. Appearance is declared in XAML, an XML-based markup whose elements become instances of WPF classes at run time, while behavior sits in code-behind linked through the x:Class attribute; the page says this separation lets designers and developers work in parallel. The framework includes many controls, a layout system with panels such as Grid, StackPanel, DockPanel, Canvas and WrapPanel, and a data binding engine connecting UI properties to data objects with validation, sorting, filtering and grouping. Graphics use device-independent pixels of 1/96 inch, with 2D, integrated 3D and animation.

x-plus-plus.title: X++ language reference (Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations)
x-plus-plus.notes: X++ is an object-oriented, application-aware and data-aware programming language used for enterprise resource planning development and database applications in Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations. The overview page lists its main features: classes, including system and application classes with reflection; access to relational tables using keywords that closely resemble SQL; manipulation of user interface items such as forms and reports; compiler best-practice checks that can raise messages; automatic garbage collection; interoperability with C# and other .NET languages; file input and output including XML; and collections such as dynamic arrays. X++ compiles to Microsoft .NET Common Intermediate Language, the same output as C# and Visual Basic. According to the page this makes code run much faster than in AX 2012 and earlier, makes it easier to integrate logic written in other managed languages, lets X++ reference classes from other .NET assemblies and allows many .NET tools to work on the result. If any method of a model element such as a class, form or query fails to compile, the whole compilation fails. The page also describes an ignore list for temporarily excluding code while porting legacy applications in stages, and warns against using it in production.

x509-certificate.title: X.509 (Wikipedia)
x509-certificate.notes: X.509 is an ITU-T standard that defines the format of public key certificates, written in ASN.1 and first published in 1988 alongside the X.500 directory standard. A certificate binds an identity, such as a hostname, organization or person, to a public key through a digital signature from a certificate authority or a self-signature. Common uses include TLS and HTTPS, S/MIME email, code signing, IPsec, EAP-TLS Wi-Fi, smart cards, TPMs and UEFI Secure Boot. A version 3 certificate holds a serial number, signature algorithm, issuer, validity period, subject, subject public key info and optional extensions, such as Basic Constraints, Key Usage and Extended Key Usage, which can be marked critical. Certificate types are root CA, intermediate CA and end-entity. To obtain one, an applicant generates a key pair and sends a certificate signing request, a registration authority validates it and the CA issues it. A chain runs from the end-entity certificate to a trust anchor, usually a self-signed root, and validation also checks dates and revocation. Revocation uses certificate revocation lists or OCSP. The page also covers weaknesses, such as hash collisions in MD5 and SHA-1, and file formats including PEM, DER, PKCS#7 and PKCS#12.

xrm-tools.title: XRM Tools documentation
xrm-tools.notes: XRM Tools is a Visual Studio extension for Power Platform development whose stated aim is to make that work feel native in Visual Studio. It adds IntelliSense for plugins, generates boilerplate code and typed entities, and lets developers control code generation with Scriban templates. Environments are added under the extension options, and a connection can use the signed-in account, a secret or a certificate; the documentation says the tool never sees or stores credentials. Plugins are written as partial classes with a Plugin attribute and Step attributes, where IntelliSense suggests messages and filters entities by table type such as standard, activity, virtual or elastic. The attributes come from the XrmTools.Meta.Attributes NuGet package, which includes their source. Saving the plugin definition file triggers the tool to read the attributes, fetch metadata from the environment and generate code with a typed Target and image properties such as PreImage. Choosing Register Plugin builds if needed and updates the assembly, its types and the step registrations in one transaction that rolls back on failure. Attributes in source are the source of truth, so registrations made with other tools are replaced.

xunit.title: xUnit.net
xunit.notes: The project page calls xUnit.net a free, open-source, community-focused unit testing tool for C#, F# and Visual Basic. Version 3 supports .NET 8.0 or later and .NET Framework 4.7.2 or later, while version 2 is in maintenance mode with only critical bug fixes and new features going to version 3. It works with the .NET SDK command line, Visual Studio, Visual Studio Code, JetBrains Rider and NCrunch, and with environments compatible with Microsoft.Testing.Platform or VSTest. It is licensed under Apache 2.0, is part of the .NET Foundation, follows a code of conduct and accepts sponsorship through GitHub Sponsors. To start, a developer installs the project templates with dotnet new install xunit.v3.templates and creates a project with dotnet new xunit3. Tests are methods marked with the Fact attribute that use Assert methods such as Assert.Equal, and they are run with dotnet run, which reports passes, failures with stack traces and a summary. Main packages are xunit.v3, xunit, xunit.analyzers and xunit.runner.visualstudio. Issues for the core framework and analyzers go to the main xunit repository, and the Visual Studio adapter has its own tracker.

yubikey.title: YubiKey (Wikipedia)
yubikey.notes: YubiKey is a line of hardware authentication devices made by Yubico, a Swedish company founded in 2007 by Jakob and Stina Ehrensvard and listed on Nasdaq Stockholm. The devices confirm user presence by a touch of the finger. Supported functions include FIDO2 and WebAuthn, where the key can store passkeys for passwordless login or act as a second factor with U2F, OATH time-based and HMAC-based one-time passwords, the PIV and OpenPGP smart card standards, and Yubico's own OTP applet, which types a code like a keyboard over USB. The YubiKey 5 Series from 2018 supports all of these in USB-A, USB-C, Lightning and NFC variants, whereas the Security Key Series is a cheaper FIDO2-only line without serial numbers. The Bio Series adds a fingerprint sensor, the YubiHSM 2 is a hardware security module for servers, and FIPS 140-2 certified variants exist for regulated customers. The article also records security notes: most firmware is closed source, a 2017 flaw in an Infineon key generation library affected some YubiKey 4 keys and Yubico replaced them for free, and a 2024 side-channel attack called EUCLEAK, which needs physical access, affects firmware before 5.7 and was rated moderate by Yubico.

mechanical-engineering.title: Mechanical engineering (Wikipedia)
mechanical-engineering.notes: Mechanical engineering is the branch of engineering that studies physical machines and mechanisms involving force and motion. It combines engineering physics, mathematics and materials science to design, analyze, manufacture and maintain mechanical systems, and it is among the oldest and broadest engineering fields. Core areas include mechanics, dynamics, thermodynamics, materials science, design and structural analysis, supported by tools such as CAD, CAM, CAE and product lifecycle management. Applications range from manufacturing plants, HVAC, vehicles, aircraft and watercraft to robotics and medical devices. The discipline took shape during the eighteenth-century Industrial Revolution, although its roots reach back thousands of years, and the Institution of Mechanical Engineers was founded in the UK in 1847 and the American Society of Mechanical Engineers in 1880. Bachelor's programs typically last four to five years. Sub-disciplines include mechanics, mechatronics, robotics, structural analysis, thermal engineering, drafting and CAD/CAM, and computer-aided engineering such as finite element analysis and computational fluid dynamics. Typical duties are analyzing problems, designing and redesigning devices, building and testing prototypes and overseeing manufacturing.

cio.title: Chief information officer (Wikipedia)
cio.notes: A chief information officer is typically the most senior executive responsible for an organization's information technology and computer systems, working to support its goals; the title is also written CDIO or IT director. The CIO usually reports to the chief executive or managing director, and some sit on the board. The role was first defined in 1981 by William Synnott and William Gruber. Responsibilities include business leadership and executive decisions on IT purchases and systems, developing the ICT strategy and policy, IT governance, cost and risk management including disaster recovery, recruitment and training, acting as the link between business needs, users and technology, overseeing vendors and outsourced services, and leading large projects such as ERP implementations and business process re-engineering. Customer-facing digital products have become part of the job in recent years. The role carries a high risk of failure, as shown by Target's CIO resigning in 2014 after a breach, and regulation such as the GDPR increased both pressure and authority. The article contrasts the CIO, focused on internal IT, with the CTO, focused on technology as external advantage, and the chief digital officer.
